In the fourth month of summer, on jiashen day, Prince Song Chengqi resigned as Minister of Works.
In the fourth month of summer, on jiashen day, Prince Song Chengqi resigned as Minister over the Masses.
司徒 is the Minister over the Masses (situ), not Minister of Works (司空); the literal field has the same error.
In the Ming era envoys were sent to inspect the ten circuits; commentators held that the Shannan circuit's jurisdiction was too broad and distant, so it was divided into eastern and western circuits.
Envoys were sent to inspect the ten circuits; commentators held that the Shannan circuit's jurisdiction was too broad and distant, so it was divided into eastern and western circuits.
明 here is not an era name (a "Ming era" is anachronistic in 711); the clause simply reports envoys sent to inspect the ten circuits.
Autumn, seventh month, guisi: Shangguan Zhaorong was posthumously rehabilitated as Huiwen.
Autumn, seventh month, guisi: the Brilliant Consort Shangguan was posthumously restored and given the posthumous name Huiwen.
昭容 is a consort rank (Brilliant Consort), not part of Shangguan's name, and 謚曰惠文 confers a posthumous name.
On yimao, a dead persimmon at the Founding Emperor's old home leafed out again; the court pardoned the empire.
On yimao, because the withered persimmon at the Founding Emperor's old residence sprouted anew, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
赦天下 is a general amnesty; "pardoned the empire" obscures the meaning, and the causal link (以) is lost.
On gengwu, Wei Anshi was named Left Vice Director of State Affairs and Crown Prince's Mentor with third-rank standing.
On gengwu, Wei Anshi, Director of the Secretariat, was named Left Vice Director of State Affairs and concurrently Guest of the Heir Apparent, with third-rank standing as chief minister.
太子賓客 is Guest (not Mentor) of the Heir Apparent, and 中書令 (Director of the Secretariat) is omitted; the literal field has the same "Mentor" error.
Wags said he had gone from the empress's father-in-law to the princess's purse-keeper.
People said Huaizhen had once been the empress's "a-die" (old dad) and was now the princess's estate steward.
阿{父者} (a-die) is a familiar term for a father figure, the nickname Dou Huaizhen earned through his tie to the empress's household, not "father-in-law"; the literal field has the same error.

Wei Anshi to Left Vice Director and Eastern Capital Commissioner; Guo Yuanzhen, Minister of Personnel; Dou Huaizhen, Left Censor-in-Chief; Li Rizhi, Minister of Revenue; Zhang Yue, Left Vice Director—all removed from power.'

Wei Anshi to Left Vice Director and Eastern Capital Commissioner; Guo Yuanzhen, Minister of Personnel; Dou Huaizhen, Left Censor-in-Chief; Li Rizhi, Minister of Revenue; Zhang Yue, Left Assistant Director—all removed from power.'
左丞 (Left Assistant Director) is distinct from 左僕射 (Left Vice Director, given to Wei Anshi in the same sentence).
Liu Youqiu became Palace Attendant; Wei Zhigu became Left Regular Attendant; Cui Shi became Vice Director of the Secretariat—all raised to third rank.

Liu Youqiu, Minister of Personnel, became Palace Attendant; Wei Zhigu, Right Regular Attendant, became Left Regular Attendant; Cui Shi, Chief Steward of the Heir Apparent, became Vice Director of the Secretariat—all made chief ministers with third-rank standing.
同中書門下三品 makes them chief ministers; "raised to third rank" misstates it, and the prior posts are omitted.
Emperor Zhongzong cast aside the founders' legacy and bent to women's will.
Emperor Zhongzong, Your Majesty's brother, cast aside the founders' legacy and bent to women's will.
陛下之兄 (Your Majesty's brother) is omitted.

When the late emperor doted on the rebel prince, Zong Jinqing built him a palace and Zhao Luwen planted gardens at ruinous cost. Palace and garden were finished before he could enjoy either—and then he was slain.

When the late emperor doted on the Rebellious Commoner, Zong Jinqing built her a mansion and Zhao Lüwen laid out her gardens at ruinous cost. Mansion and garden were finished before she could enjoy either—and then she was executed.
悖逆 is the Rebellious Commoner, the late emperor's indulged daughter, not a "rebel prince"; pronouns must be feminine. The literal field has the same error.
He Fengyao, Vice Censor and acting Director of Banquets, told Mo-chuo: 'Once Chumiji and Jiankun hear you have wed the Tang court, they will come over.

He Fengyao, Vice Censor-in-Chief and acting Chief Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, was sent as envoy to the Turks and told Mochuo: 'Once the Chumiji and Jiankun hear you have made a marriage alliance with Tang, they will all submit.
使於突厥 (sent as envoy to the Turks) is omitted, and 鴻臚卿 is the Chief Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, not "Director of Banquets"; the literal field has the same title error.

Mo-chuo consented. The next day he donned Tang dress, bowed toward the south, declared himself a vassal, and sent his son Yang Wuzhi and his chancellor to court with Fengyao. Eleventh month, wuyin: they reached the capital.

Mo-chuo consented. The next day he donned Tang dress, bowed toward the south, declared himself a vassal, and sent his son Yang Wozhi and his chancellor to court with Fengyao. Eleventh month, wuyin: they reached the capital.
楊我支 is Yang Wozhi (我 wo), as spelled in s0267; the literal field has the same "Wuzhi" misspelling.
In the twelfth month, on guimao, Ashina Xian—the exiled Khan of Xingxi—was named envoy to win over the Ten Surname tribes.
In the twelfth month, on guimao, Ashina Xian, the Xingxiwang Qaghan, was named Commissioner to Summon and Pacify the Ten Surnames.
興昔亡可汗 is a fixed Western Turkic title (Xingxiwang Qaghan), not "the exiled Khan of Xingxi"; the literal field has the same misreading ("khan of Xingxi who had fled").
In spring, the first month, on xinsi, Emperor Ruizong offered sacrifice at the Southern Suburb, inaugurating the joint rite of Heaven and Earth as urged by Remonstrance and Counselor Jia Zeng.

In spring, the first month, on xinsi, Emperor Ruizong offered sacrifice at the Southern Suburb, for the first time adopting the joint sacrifice to Heaven and Earth proposed by Jia Zeng, Grand Master of Remonstrance.
諫議大夫 is the office Grand Master of Remonstrance; "Remonstrance and Counselor" garbles it, and the literal field has the same error.
He fell out with Li Jin, prefect of Yanzhou. Jin denounced him to Liu Youqiu, who recommended Left General of the Feathered Forest Sun Wan to take his place.
He fell out with Li Jin, prefect of Yanzhou. Jin denounced him to Liu Youqiu, who recommended Left General of the Feathered Forest Sun Quan to take his place.
孫佺 is Sun Quan (佺 quan), not "Sun Wan"; the literal field has the same error.
In the third month, on dingchou, Sun Wan was appointed Great Protector-General of Youzhou, and Xue Ne was reassigned as chief secretary of Bingzhou.
In the third month, on dingchou, Sun Quan was appointed Great Protector-General of Youzhou, and Xue Ne was reassigned as chief secretary of Bingzhou.
佺 is read quan: Sun Quan, not "Sun Wan"; the literal field has the same error ("Wan").
In recognition of Cen Xi's service in shielding the throne during the turmoil of Crown Prince Jiemin, on guichou the emperor appointed him Vice Director of the Secretariat.
In recognition of Cen Xi's service in shielding the throne during the turmoil of Crown Prince Jiemin, on guichou the emperor appointed him Palace Attendant.
侍中 is Palace Attendant, head of the Chancellery, not Vice Director of the Secretariat (中書侍郎); the literal field has the same error.
On gengshen, Sun Wan, Great Protector-General of Youzhou, clashed with the Xi chieftain Li Dapu at Cold Gorge Pass—and his whole force was annihilated.
On gengshen, Sun Quan, Great Protector-General of Youzhou, clashed with the Xi chieftain Li Dapu at Lengxing—and his whole force was annihilated.
孫佺 is Sun Quan (佺 quan), not "Sun Wan", and 冷陘 is Lengxing; the literal field has the same name error and writes "Lengyu".

By then Sun Wan had marched under Left General of the Vigorous Guard Li Kailuo and Left General of the Awe-Inspiring Guard Zhou Yiti with twenty thousand foot soldiers and eight thousand horsemen, split into three columns, to strike the Xi and Khitan.

By then Sun Quan was leading Li Kailuo, Left General of the Valiant Guard, and Zhou Yiti, Left General of the Awe-Inspiring Guard, with twenty thousand foot soldiers and eight thousand horsemen, split into three columns, to strike the Xi and Khitan.
佺帥… means Sun Quan led the two generals, not that he "marched under" them; 孫佺 is Sun Quan, and the literal field has the same "Wan" error.
Sun Wan replied: 'Xue Ne held the border for years and still could not win back Yingzhou for the empire.'
Sun Quan replied: 'Xue Ne held the border for years and still could not win back Yingzhou for the empire.'
佺 (Sun Quan) is read quan, not "Wan"; the literal field has the same error.
Sun Wan, too cowardly to reinforce him, began to withdraw—and the enemy pressed hard, routing the Tang army.
Sun Quan, too cowardly to reinforce him, began to withdraw—and the enemy pressed hard, routing the Tang army.
佺 (Sun Quan) is read quan, not "Wan"; the literal field has the same error.
Sun Wan drew up a square formation against the hills to hold his ground. Li Dapu sent a messenger: 'Your court has already bound us in marriage alliance—why does a great army come now?'
Sun Quan drew up a square formation against the hills to hold his ground. Li Dapu sent a messenger: 'Your court has already bound us in marriage alliance—why does a great army come now?'
佺 (Sun Quan) is read quan, not "Wan"; the literal field has the same error.
Sun Wan answered: 'I come only under imperial command to offer reassurance and goodwill.
Sun Quan answered: 'I come only under imperial command to offer reassurance and goodwill.
佺 (Sun Quan) is read quan, not "Wan"; the literal field has the same error.
Sun Wan collected every bolt of silk in the camp—more than ten thousand in all—along with purple robes, gold belts, and official fish purses, and sent them as gifts.
Sun Quan collected every bolt of silk in the camp—more than ten thousand in all—along with purple robes, gold belts, and official fish purses, and sent them as gifts.
佺 (Sun Quan) is read quan, not "Wan"; the literal field has the same error.
Sun Wan and Zhou Yiti were taken captive, handed over to the Turks, and Khaghan Moqur put them both to death;
Sun Quan and Zhou Yiti were taken captive, handed over to the Turks, and Mochuo put them both to death;
佺 is Sun Quan, not "Sun Wan", and 默啜 is Mochuo, not "Khaghan Moqur"; the literal field has the same name error and writes "Mo-chu".
On renyin, the Great Sage Empress Dowager was styled Sage-Emperor Empress Dowager.
On renyin, the posthumous title of Wu Zetian, Great Sage Heavenly Empress, was raised to Sage Emperor Heavenly Empress.
大聖天後 is Wu Zetian's posthumous title (Heavenly Empress), not an "Empress Dowager"; 上…尊號 means the title was raised. The literal field has the same "Empress Dowager" error.
Liu Youqiu became Right Vice Director and third-rank co-chancellor; Wei Zhigu, Attendant-in-Chief; Cui Shi, acting Grand Counselor.
Liu Youqiu became Right Vice Director of State Affairs and Fellow Chief Minister of the Third Rank; Wei Zhigu, Palace Attendant; Cui Shi, acting Director of the Secretariat.
侍中 is Palace Attendant and 中書令 is Director of the Secretariat, not "Attendant-in-Chief" and "Grand Counselor"; the literal field has the same errors.
The empress was childless; Lady Yang raised the boy.
Empress Wang had no son and raised him as her own.
王后無子，母養之 means the childless Empress Wang raised Sisheng as a mother; the subject is the empress, not Lady Yang.

On jiawu, Song Jing, prefect of Youzhou, became Grand Commander of the Left Army; Xue Ne, chief secretary of Bingzhou, Grand Commander of the Central Army and Grand Protector of Shuofang; Guo Yuanzhen, Minister of War, Grand Commander of the Right Army.

On jiawu, Song Jing, Area Commander of Youzhou, became Grand Commander of the Left Army; Xue Ne, chief secretary of Bingzhou, Grand Commander of the Central Army; and Guo Yuanzhen, Grand Commander of Shuofang and Minister of War, Grand Commander of the Right Army.
朔方大總管 goes with 兵部尚書郭元振 (Guo Yuanzhen's existing posts), not with Xue Ne; 都督 is Area Commander, not prefect. The literal field has the same misattribution.
Xiao Zhibo, Minister of the Civil Service, was made Grand Counselor.
Xiao Zhizhong, Minister of Personnel, was made Director of the Secretariat.
蕭至忠 is Xiao Zhizhong, not "Xiao Zhibo"; 中書令 is Director of the Secretariat. The literal field has the same name error.
Now Zuorong was made Left Cavalry Guard General and Prince of Bohai;
Now Zuorong was made Grand General of the Left Valiant Guard and Commandery Prince of Bohai;
左驍衛大將軍 is Grand General of the Left Valiant Guard, and 渤海郡王 is a commandery prince; the literal field has the same "Left Cavalry Guard General" error.

With Dou Huaizhen, Cen Xi, Xiao Zhizhong, Cui Shi, Heir Apparent Grand Mentor Xue Ji, Yong Prefecture chief administrator Prince Jin of Xinxing, Left Feathered Forest General Chang Yuankai, acting Right Feathered Forest commander Li Ci, Left Golden Guard General Li Qin, drafting officer Li You, Right Regular Attendant Jia Yingfu, Chamberlain for Dependencies Tang Jun, and the monk Huifan she plotted to depose the emperor and raise another. With the palace woman Lady Yuan she also schemed to lace arrowroot powder with poison and serve it to the throne.

With Dou Huaizhen, Cen Xi, Xiao Zhizhong, Cui Shi, Xue Ji, Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Yong Prefecture chief administrator Prince Jin of Xinxing, Left Feathered Forest General Chang Yuankai, acting Right Feathered Forest commander Li Ci, Left Golden Guard General Li Qin, drafting officer Li You, Right Regular Attendant Jia Yingfu, Chamberlain for Dependencies Tang Jun, and the monk Huifan she plotted to depose the emperor and raise another. With the palace woman Lady Yuan she also schemed to lace arrowroot powder with poison and serve it to the throne.
太子少保 is Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, not "Grand Mentor"; the literal field has the same error.
On bingchen day Turkic khan Moqie sent his son Yang Wozhi to sue for a bride;
On bingchen day the Turkic qaghan Mochuo sent his son Yang Wozhi to sue for a bride;
默啜 is Mochuo (Qapaghan Qaghan), not "Moqie"; the literal field has the same error.

The emperor then joined with Princes Fan of Qi and Ye of Xue, Guo Yuanzhen, and Longwu General Wang Maoqi, Palace Supervisor Assistant Jiang Jiao, Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Li Lingwen, Palace Stud Attendant Wang Shouyi, Inner Palace Supply Officer Gao Lishi, and Guardsman Li Shoude and others to fix a plan to execute them.

The emperor then joined with Princes Fan of Qi and Ye of Xue, Guo Yuanzhen, and Longwu General Wang Maozhong, Palace Supervisor Assistant Jiang Jiao, Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud Li Lingwen, Palace Stud Attendant Wang Shouyi, Inner Palace Supply Officer Gao Lishi, and Guardsman Li Shoude and others to fix a plan to execute them.
王毛仲 is Wang Maozhong; the idiomatic field is correct, but the literal field writes "Wang Maoqi".

On jiazi, the emperor through Wang Maoqi took spare-stable horses and more than three hundred soldiers, together with more than ten fellow conspirators, entered from Wude Hall through Qianhua Gate, summoned Yuankai and Ci, and beheaded them first; he seized Yingfu and You in the Inner Reception Office and brought them out, arrested Zhizhong and Xi in the audience hall, and beheaded them all.

On jiazi, the emperor through Wang Maozhong took spare-stable horses and more than three hundred soldiers, together with more than ten fellow conspirators, entered from Wude Hall through Qianhua Gate, summoned Yuankai and Ci, and beheaded them first; he seized Yingfu and You in the Inner Reception Office and brought them out, arrested Zhizhong and Xi in the audience hall, and beheaded them all.
王毛仲 is Wang Maozhong; the idiomatic field is correct, but the literal field writes "Wang Maoqi".
Liu Youqiu and Zhang Shuo knelt before the imperial horse and pleaded: "Yuanzhen has served the realm with great merit — he cannot be put to death."
Liu Youqiu and Zhang Yue knelt before the imperial horse and pleaded: "Yuanzhen has served the realm with great merit — he cannot be put to death."
張說 is Zhang Yue (說 read yue in his name), not "Zhang Shuo"; the literal field has the same misreading.
The emperor wished to make Tongzhou Governor Yao Yuanzhi chancellor; Zhang Shuo, who resented him, had Censor-in-chief Zhao Yanzhao bring charges, but the emperor would not heed them.
The emperor wished to make Tongzhou Governor Yao Yuanzhi chancellor; Zhang Yue, who resented him, had Censor-in-chief Zhao Yanzhao bring charges, but the emperor would not heed them.
張說 is Zhang Yue (說 read yue in his name), not "Zhang Shuo"; the literal field has the same misreading.
The emperor said, "This is Zhang Shuo's scheme. How dare you lie to my face — the punishment is death!"
The emperor said, "This is Zhang Yue's scheme. How dare you lie to my face — the punishment is death!"
張說 is Zhang Yue (說 read yue in his name), not "Zhang Shuo"; the literal field has the same misreading.
After Yao Chong became chancellor, Purple Palace Secretariat Director Zhang Shuo grew fearful and secretly went to pay court to the Prince of Qi.
After Yao Chong became chancellor, Purple Palace Secretariat Director Zhang Yue grew fearful and secretly went to pay court to the Prince of Qi.
張說 is Zhang Yue (說 read yue in his name), not "Zhang Shuo"; the literal field has the same misreading.

He said, "The Prince of Qi is Your Majesty's beloved brother; Zhang Shuo is a chief minister, yet he secretly rode into the princely house in a carriage. I fear Your Majesty's brother may be led astray — that is my trouble."

He said, "The Prince of Qi is Your Majesty's beloved brother; Zhang Yue is a chief minister, yet he secretly rode into the princely house in a carriage. I fear Your Majesty's brother may be led astray — that is my trouble."
張說 is Zhang Yue (說 read yue in his name), not "Zhang Shuo"; the literal field has the same misreading.
On guichou day Zhang Shuo was demoted to prefect of Xiangzhou.
On guichou day Zhang Yue was demoted to prefect of Xiangzhou.
張說 is Zhang Yue (說 read yue in his name), not "Zhang Shuo"; the literal field has the same misreading.
Attendant-in-ordinary Tang Shao, who oversaw ritual protocol, was beheaded for failing to keep the military rites in proper order.
Tang Shao, Supervising Secretary in charge of ritual protocol, was beheaded for failing to keep the military rites in proper order.
給事中 is Supervising Secretary of the Chancellery, not "Attendant-in-ordinary"; the literal field has the same error.
Right Vice Director Liu Youqiu, Associate of the Three Departments, was also dismissed and made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
Right Vice Director Liu Youqiu, Fellow Chief Minister of the Third Rank, was also dismissed and made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
太子少保 is Junior Guardian (保), not "Junior Tutor" (少傅); the literal field has the same error.
